name: Heatless curls

card.summary: A way of curling or waving hair overnight by wrapping it around a rod, cloth or similar form instead of using a hot tool, for curls without heat styling.
card.note: Avoids hot tools, which can damage hair with overuse; results vary with hair type.

quick.overview:
Heatless curling shapes hair into curls or waves without a curling iron. Damp or dry hair is wrapped around a form and left to set, often overnight, so that it dries or relaxes in a curled shape.

It is popular as a way to get volume and curl while skipping the heat of irons, which reference sources say can cause severe damage with overuse.
quick.how: Hair is wrapped around a soft rod, cloth strip, roller or similar form and secured, then left to set before the form is removed. Many people do it before sleeping and style the curls afterward.
quick.risks: No heat damage is involved, though sleeping with wrapped hair can be uncomfortable, and tight wrapping can tug on hair. Curl hold varies by hair type and weather.

lead: Heatless curls are curls or waves set without a hot tool, typically by wrapping hair around a soft form and leaving it to set, often overnight. Heated curling irons, by comparison, come in barrels roughly 0.5 to 2 inches wide and produce curls from spiral ringlets to larger waves.[1]
The appearance goal is the same as with an iron: curl, wave and volume. The draw of the heatless route is avoiding heat styling, because overuse of heated tools can cause severe damage to hair.[1]
No clinical studies have examined heatless curling methods. The topic is mainly a matter of styling practice.

angle.text: The method produces curls and waves overnight, and is chosen by people who want styled hair while limiting use of heated tools.

paras: Heatless curling shapes hair by wrapping it around a form and letting it set. Heated tools, including curling irons and straighteners, alter hair shape with heat; straighteners, for instance, break hydrogen bonds in the cortex, which can re-form with moisture.[1]
The reference article on hair curling notes that overuse of heated tools can cause severe damage to hair.[1] People who style frequently may use a no-heat method to reduce that exposure.
